headline: Plant and cross-species databases integrate multi-omics evidence for transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulation
label: Plant Regulatory Omics Resources
summary: New database releases and an isoform atlas extend regulatory annotation in plants and model species, spanning miRNAs, cis-regulatory networks, RBP sites and isoform QTLs.
synthesis: The current items converge on regulatory-layer resources, mostly for plants, not on the gut microbiome. PmiREN3.0 integrates multi-omics data for plant miRNA research, and PlantPAN 5.0 updates cis-regulatory and transcriptional network coverage to 240 species. oRNAment V2 expands putative RBP target-site predictions across transcriptomes of diverse model species. The lettuce preprint adds a population-scale pan-isoform atlas and the ISONET-GWAS framework, which maps traits at isoform level and identifies trans-sQTL hotspots near LsPPR. Together they show regulatory annotation moving from gene-level to isoform-, miRNA-, RBP- and network-level evidence. The summaries do not support any gut-specific claim.
